evidence.quote: Conducts business in Washington, or produces or provides products or services that are targeted to consumers in Washington

summary.short: Washington statute regulating collection, sharing and sale of consumer health data by regulated entities and small businesses. Requires privacy policies, consent, consumer rights and signed authorization for sales; prohibits certain geofences around health care facilities. Most duties apply from March 31, 2024; small businesses from June 30, 2024.
summary.long: Washington's My Health My Data Act (Laws of 2023, ch. 191) regulates consumer health data collected, shared or sold in Washington. Regulated entities and small businesses must publish a consumer health data privacy policy, obtain consent before collecting or sharing such data, and avoid unlawful discrimination against consumers exercising rights. Access must be restricted, data secured, and processors bound by contracts. Consumers may access, delete and withdraw consent over their data, with a 45-day response period and appeal rights. Selling consumer health data requires a signed valid authorization meeting listed requirements, expiring after one year. Sellers and purchasers keep authorizations for six years. Geofencing around in-person health care services to track consumers or send them health-related messages is unlawful. Violations are unfair or deceptive acts under the Consumer Protection Act. HIPAA-protected and other specified information is exempt. A joint legislative committee reviews enforcement actions; that section expires June 30, 2031. Most duties apply from March 31, 2024; small businesses from June 30, 2024.

"Consumer" means (a) a natural person who is a Washington resident; or (b) a natural person whose consumer health data is collected in Washington.
"Consumer health data" means personal information that is linked or reasonably linkable to a consumer and that identifies the consumer's past, present, or future physical or mental health status.
"Regulated entity" means any legal entity that: (a) Conducts business in Washington, or produces or provides products or services that are targeted to consumers in Washington
"Small business" means a regulated entity that satisfies one or both of the following thresholds:
"Processor" means a person that processes consumer health data on behalf of a regulated entity or a small business.
"Person" does not include government agencies, tribal nations, or contracted service providers when processing consumer health data on behalf of a government agency.
"Third party" means an entity other than a consumer, regulated entity, processor, small business, or affiliate of the regulated entity or the small business.
"Affiliate" means a legal entity that shares common branding with another legal entity and controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with another legal entity.
"Sell" or "sale" means the exchange of consumer health data for monetary or other valuable consideration.
"Share" or "sharing" means to release, disclose, disseminate, divulge, make available, provide access to, license, or otherwise communicate orally, in writing, or by electronic or other means
"Collect" means to buy, rent, access, retain, receive, acquire, infer, derive, or otherwise process consumer health data in any manner.
"Consent" means a clear affirmative act that signifies a consumer's freely given, specific, informed, opt-in, voluntary, and unambiguous agreement
"Deceptive design" means a user interface designed or manipulated with the effect of subverting or impairing user autonomy, decision making, or choice.

"Geofence" means technology that uses global positioning coordinates, cell tower connectivity, cellular data, radio frequency identification, Wifi data, and/or any other form of spatial or location detection to establish a virtual boundary around a specific physical location
"Precise location information" means information derived from technology including, but not limited to, global positioning system level latitude and longitude coordinates or other mechanisms
"Personal information" means information that identifies or is reasonably capable of being associated or linked, directly or indirectly, with a particular consumer.
"Publicly available information" means information that (a) is lawfully made available through federal, state, or municipal government records or widely distributed media
"Deidentified data" means data that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, an identified or identifiable consumer

obligations.summary: Maintain a consumer health data privacy policy clearly and conspicuously disclosing categories of data and purposes, sources, categories shared, categories of third parties and affiliates, and how consumers exercise rights; prominently publish a homepage link to it.

obligations.summary: Process consumer health data only under a binding contract setting processing instructions and limiting actions, and only consistent with those instructions; assist the regulated entity or small business with technical and organizational measures to meet its obligations. obligations.summary: Unlawful to sell or offer to sell consumer health data without first obtaining a valid authorization signed by the consumer, separate from collection or sharing consent. The authorization must contain the items in Sec. 9(2)(a)-(i), cannot be conditioned on goods or services, and a copy must be given to the consumer.
